answers.core: It's technically already implemented (because you can see the bounding box in the editor when selected). Although the use cases are probably not that high, the bounding box is pretty general.
answers.workaround: Well, not that easy, but I found a [Reddit post](https://www.reddit.com/r/godot/comments/18bfn0n/how_to_calculate_node3d_bounding_box/), which also roughly describes the problem. It does contain multiple solutions, but it also has some decent lines of code.

title: Add a way to get the bounding box of any 3D Node including its children (like shown in the editor)
